findings.title: `include_website_name` is missing the trailing `?` so it will never be called as a guard
findings.body: ActiveModel::Serializer recognizes conditional inclusion methods by the naming convention `include_<attribute>?` (with a question mark). The method is defined as `include_website_name` without the `?`, so the serializer framework will never invoke it as a guard. As a result, `website_name` will always be serialized (as `null` when website is blank) rather than being omitted. Rename to `include_website_name?` to match the convention.

findings.title: `website_name` is not listed in `untrusted_attributes`, leaking info for TL0 users to anonymous viewers
findings.body: The `website` attribute is listed in `untrusted_attributes` (line 109), which hides it from anonymous users viewing TL0 profiles. However, `website_name` is only in the regular `attributes` list and is not added to `untrusted_attributes`. This means anonymous visitors can still see the website name (and potentially the full path) for TL0 users even though the raw `website` URL is hidden. Add `:website_name` to the `untrusted_attributes` call to maintain consistent visibility rules.

findings.title: Test for untrusted attributes does not include `website_name`
findings.body: The `untrusted_attributes` list in the spec (line 11) does not include `:website_name`. Since `website_name` should be hidden for TL0 users seen by anonymous viewers (same as `website`), it should be added to this list so the test verifies it is properly suppressed. Without this, the missing `untrusted_attributes` entry in the serializer goes undetected.

findings.title: `URI(website.to_s)` is parsed multiple times redundantly
findings.body: The `website_name` method calls `URI(website.to_s)` up to four times (lines 138, 143, 146, 149). Parsing the URI once into a local variable at the top of the method and reusing it would be clearer and avoid redundant parsing, especially since this runs on every user profile serialization.
